Thanks Ellen — received the workbook and good questions. Summarizing two pragmatic paths we typically propose for customers like CloudWay:

Option A — Starter retainer (recommended for predictable pilots):
- One-time implementation SOW (fixed fee) covering install, network integration, and one HA site.
- 6-month SRE retainer (monthly) to cover runbook handoff, post-cutover stabilization, and emergency response.
- Platform fee (annualized) that covers console, model catalog, and observability; amortized monthly in billing.
- Migration credit: We apply a one-time credit equal to 25% of implementation fee if you convert to a 12-month committed Dedicated contract within 9 months.

Option B — Metered ops model (recommended for flexible consumption):
- Lower implementation fee (reduced scope), monthly metered charge for platform usage (per-token/metric) + ops charge based on SLOs.
- No migration credit by default; we can add a conversion credit if you commit to year 2.

Key SLA/credits behavior:
- If throughput < committed baseline during first 3 months: no penalty, we revisit sizing.
- If downtime triggers SLA credit per contract, credits apply to platform fee and ops retainer proportionally.

I'll loop Marissa for concrete numbers and an example invoice cadence. Would you prefer a 6- or 12-month amortization for the platform fee in the invoice sample?

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Adding a quick ops/engineering perspective to clarify how credits and scaling behave — helps avoid surprises with finance.

1) Migration credit mechanics:
- Credit is triggered by a signed amendment to move to a 12-month Dedicated commitment. Customer-side claim is possible but we prefer the automatic credit at first invoice post-amendment. We record the credit on the first billing cycle after the amendment is processed.

2) Multi-site scale/pro-rating:
- If you add sites in month 9, we pro-rate operator seat charges and platform-fee delta for the remainder of the amortization window. Migration credit remains valid as long as the Dedicated amendment executes within the contractual window (9 months).

3) SLA credit flow:
- SLA credits are applied to the following invoice cycle and capped at a % of monthly platform + ops charges as defined in SOW. Implementation SOW is not refundable via SLA credits.

Operational note: we can also offer a short-term trial burst credit (one month token credit up to $25k) for proof-of-concept if that helps unblock legal.

I'm available to join procurement call Thursday if helpful.
